references.text: God promises that He will give rain at the right time and that the land will yield its produce, which supports the promise of blessing in the sixth year.
The Lord promises to send blessing over the storehouses and all labor, corresponding to the promise of a triple harvest.
God opens His rich treasury and gives rain to the land at the right time, expressing the same principle of divine blessing over the crop.
On the sixth day, the Israelites gathered double the amount of manna, illustrating the same principle of God's provision before a rest period.
God gives a double portion on the sixth day before the Sabbath, parallel to the promise of a triple harvest before the sabbatical year.
Jesus teaches that when one seeks God's kingdom first, all necessary things will be given in addition, reflecting trust in God's provision during the sabbatical year.
Paul assures that God will give everything needed according to His riches, expressing the same trust in God's provision.
During the seven years of abundance, the land yielded a plentiful harvest, demonstrating God's ability to provide abundance to sustain future years.
